record.field:
The employee master form, read with sIndex/limit=200 pagination and dateFormat=yyyy-MM-dd.
This row shipped as `forms/P_Employee/records`, which Zoho does not serve: it answers HTTP 200 with the body `[{"message":"Invalid View Name", "errorcode":7012,"Response status":2}]`. The connector's error handling read that as data, crashed on it, swallowed the crash and reported a successful pull of zero employees — and because every other Zoho feed is a per-employee lookup driven by the stored employee list, all seven feeds then read empty. Corrected to the path the legacy ABM application always used, and verified against a live tenant on 2026-08-26. Migration 19.0.1.84.0 repairs installed databases.
The legacy ABM application read the SAME data from this endpoint, with dateFormat=yyyy-MM-dd and no pagination at all — one call, first 200 records (om_hr_payroll/models/hr_zoho_staging.py:309). Its dependent count came from this record's `tabularSections` → "Dependent and Dependent Health Insurance" (:367-373), which is why the DEPCOUNT transformation rule reads employee rows and not dependent rows.

Per-employee attendance totals for a date window (om_hr_payroll/models/hr_zoho_staging.py:456). The join key is `emailId`, NOT the employee id — the legacy code matched its staging rows on email (:465).
Two payload shapes in one response, and the difference costs an hour if it is not written down: `expectedWorkingHours` and `totalWorkedHours` arrive in SECONDS, while `paidLeaveHours` arrives as an "H:MM" string. The WORKEDHRS transformation rule reproduces the legacy arithmetic (paidLeaveSeconds + totalWorkedHours) / 3600.

Approved overtime, banded by OT_Type (150% / 200% / 210% / 270% / 300% / 390%) with the payable hours in `Actual_Pay_Hour` (om_hr_payroll/models/hr_zoho_staging.py:472-485).
The proven request contract searches on EMPLOYEEMAILALIAS, so the runtime keeps the legacy per-employee request pattern (:471). That is deliberately visible in the parameter note: it is rate-limit-sensitive and should only be replaced once a tenant has verified that its Zoho form accepts a safe window-only call. The OTHRS* rules carry no date filter of their own because the API call already scopes every response to the payroll window (:497-557).

The salary form, looked up by the employee's Zoho record id (integrations/zoho_connector.py, `_get_employee_salary`). Not used by the legacy ABM application, which took pay from the payroll spreadsheet rather than Zoho.
This row shipped as `forms/P_Salary/records`. There is no form called `P_Salary` — Zoho rejects the name outright ("Form name 'P_Salary' is invalid"), and the `/records` suffix returns the same silent "Invalid View Name" body that broke the employee feed. The tenant's link name is `salary_details`; verified live 2026-08-26 and repaired on installed databases by migration 19.0.1.84.0.
sIndex, limit=200 (paginated), dateFormat=yyyy-MM-dd; the payroll window is applied by this platform, not by Zoho

The leave form.
Two earlier paths were wrong here. `api/v2/leavetracker/leaves/records` was dormant, and the 19.0.1.59.0 migration replaced it with `leave/getLeaveDetails` — which Zoho answers with 404 "Incorrect URL". Both are per-employee shapes, and Zoho People has no per-employee leave API on this plan: leave is a FORM, read whole.
So this feed reads the form and filters to the payroll window itself, on From/To. Zoho's form search accepts searchField=From&searchOperator=Between and then ignores it — a January-2020 window returns the same first page as no window at all — so a server-side filter here would be a filter that silently does nothing. Verified live 2026-08-26; `Employee_ID.ID` carries the employee's Zoho record id and is the join key.
empId (the employee NUMBER) or emailId, sdate, edate, dateFormat=dd-MM-yyyy

Day-by-day punches for one employee. The summary report above is the feed a payroll run wants; this one is for looking at a single person's days when a number is disputed.
This row shipped as `attendance/getAttendanceByDate`, which Zoho answers with 404 "Incorrect URL". The live path is `attendance/getUserReport`, and its `empId` is the employee NUMBER from the employee form (EmployeeID, e.g. 11708) — given the Zoho record id (811648…) it answers HTTP 200 with `{"error":"Invalid User."}`, so the connector passes the number, falling back to emailId. The response is keyed by date rather than being a list. Verified live 2026-08-26; repaired by migration 19.0.1.84.0.
user (email address, required), fromDate, toDate, dateFormat=dd-MM-yyyy

The time tracker. Catalogued because the legacy code names it (om_hr_payroll/models/hr_zoho.py:182) — but it names it in a COMMENTED-OUT line, immediately replaced by the attendance summary report. Nothing has ever called it in production here, so its default execution stays Catalogue only.
Its parameters are no longer unverified: without `user` it answers HTTP 200 with "No user parameter specified.", and with an email address in `user` it answers an empty result on a tenant that does not use time tracking (verified live 2026-08-26). The connector implements it as a per-employee call by email, so a tenant that does use it can switch this feed to Executable.
POST body: page, page_size=200, api_key, datasetKey

Employee master data (integrations/darwin_connector.py:48). POST, not GET: Darwinbox carries its credentials and its paging in the JSON body, so the "parameters" above are body keys rather than a query string.
Darwinbox can also PUSH: an inbound webhook is served at /api/darwin/webhook, which is a route rather than a feed and therefore has no row of its own.
POST body: employee_ids, date range, api_key, datasetKey
Salary and compensation for a set of employees over a date range (integrations/darwin_connector.py:49).
